title: Oncall Calm Protocol and Tiered Signal Synthesis
creator: Aisha Malik
description: Problem: Our on-call team is repeatedly paged for transient, low-impact SLO noise across regions during short-lived load spikes. These pages increase cognitive load and slow remediation for real regressions. Goal: Implement a tiered signal synthesis layer that reduces noise at the alerting surface, pairs alert tiers with explicit on-call playbooks, and automates first-line mitigation actions for common transient states (soft shedding, short-lived KV cache misses, and model variant fallbacks). This initiative ties SLO signal semantics directly to a graded runbook and automated remediation pipeline so humans see high-confidence events and the system handles common transient failures.
acceptance_criteria: >50% reduction in P1-worthy pages for transient failures on staging canary traffic
New synthesized alert tiers (Info/Watch/Action) are visible in the console and map to runbooks
Automated soft-shedding action can be triggered by the alerting layer and rolls back on signal dilution
Runbook templates are added to the on-call handbook and validated in a fire-drill
Post-rollout: no effect on user-facing SLOs (less than 0.5% additional error budget consumption)
Instrumentation: per-alert precision/recall metrics emitted to reliability dashboard
implementation_notes: Three main components: 1) Signal Synthesizer (aggregation + scoring) — accepts raw signals (latency, tail token time, region error rate, queue length) and emits a tiered score with decay windows. 2) Tiered Alert Router — maps scores to alerting destinations (Slack channel, PagerDuty routing with reduced escalation, oncall flow) and triggers automated mitigations for mid-tier events. 3) Runbook & Automation Library — canned playbook steps that can be executed automatically (e.g., enable short-term KV cache bypass, route traffic away from region, switch to cheaper model variant, transient scaling). We'll implement synthesizer as a service behind the observability stack (Prometheus/OTel input, rules in Synth service), and the router will use a thin policy engine (Rego-lite) for mapping to PagerDuty/console tags.
progress_updates: 2026-02-19: Kickoff — aligned on scope with SRE, Product, and Console teams. Agreed to phase rollout (staging -> prod-canary -> global).
2026-02-24: Prototype synthesizer rules implemented in staging; initial scoring uses exponentially-weighted decay with a 2-minute half-life for transient latencies.
2026-02-26: Ran 48h replay against last three incidents — reduced noisy pages by 57% in replay while preserving detection for major outages. False negatives reviewed with incident owners.
2026-03-01: PR opened for Synth service core (github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/3121). Console team prepping UI slot for tiered labels. Oncall handbook draft uploaded to Confluence.
decision_log: Use time-decayed scoring to distinguish transient spikes from sustained regressions (decision date: 2026-02-20)

Automated mitigations limited to non-destructive, reversible actions for mid-tier signals (decision date: 2026-02-22): e.g., short token-batched shedding, model variant fallback, region routing advice — not full-scale drain.
PagerDuty routing for Action tier will continue to page primary on-call; Watch tier will create a ticket + notify secondary channel to avoid interrupting primary (decision date: 2026-02-25)
Rollbacks: synth rules can be toggled by region via the console feature flag; initial rollout uses conservative thresholds for EU region (decision date: 2026-02-28)
runbook_excerpt: 1) Watch tier alert: note region and score; check synth score decay. If score < Action threshold: annotate ticket and set 10m watch timer. 2) If score persists > Action threshold for 3 consecutive windows: run automated mitigation step A (enable soft-shedding for 2m). 3) Observe: if SLOs stabilize (latency P95 back to baseline), auto-reverse mitigation. 4) If not stabilized or error rates rising, escalate to primary on-call and execute regional reroute play (runbook step: invoke traffic-shift script with safety checks). 5) Post-incident: attach synth score timeline to incident and run regression test on a synthetic workload.
rollback_plan: Feature-flagged synthesizer with region-level toggles. Rollback by setting synth mode to 'passthrough' which forwards raw signals to existing alerting rules. Default backoff: immediate for staging; 10-minute cool-down for prod to avoid flapping. Communicate rollback in #oncall-ops and mark in change log.
testing_plan: Unit tests for Synth scoring functions with synthetic distributions
Replay test: run replay pipeline against last 90 days of alerts and measure page reduction and detection latency
Canary: enable synth in staging and prod-canary region for 72h; run two scheduled fire-drills
Chaos test: simulate region short-term saturation to validate automated mitigation and rollback behavior
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): enable synth in staging — 2026-03-03 to 2026-03-07
Phase 2 (prod-canary region us-west-2): enable with conservative thresholds for 72h and run fire-drill — target 2026-03-10
Phase 3: enable globally with incremental threshold relaxation over two weeks; monitor precision/recall metrics daily
Post-rollout: schedule 1-week retrospective and iterate on rule sets
monitoring_playback: Emit metrics: synth.score.histogram, synth.alert_count_by_tier, synth.automated_mitigation_count, synth.false_positive_rate. Create Grafana panel showing side-by-side timeline of raw signal vs synthesized tier for oncall review. Alert when mitigation_count spikes > baseline * 2 within 15m.
notes: Make sure product teams are aware of Watch-tier tickets being created automatically to avoid duplicate investigations. We'll publish a short training doc and run a 30m oncall walkthrough before prod-canary activation.
next_steps: Merge PR for synth core, coordinate console tag slot with ENG-41234, schedule staging enablement, and run the first fire-drill with SRE on 2026-03-04.
